product.name: RunContainer
product.purpose: A Windows launcher that gives each imported executable its own folder, its own redirected profile and a verified isolation engine, so apps do not mix with each other or install into the rest of the PC.

components.role: Electron renderer. Installs apps, starts/stops them, shows state, logs and repair actions. Never launches anything itself.
Electron main process. Owns the app store under userData, selects an engine, launches and verifies processes, runs the behavioural monitor, and performs repairs through structured actions.

Default containment engine on every Windows 10/11 edition: a suspended process start, Job Object assignment (kill-on-close, memory/CPU/process caps), resume, and per-app redirected profile folders. Verified in-job after launch. NOT a virtual machine and does not cut network access.
Optional Windows AppContainer token for compatible apps. Verified container SID. Cannot run installers, drivers or services that need administrator rights. NOT a virtual machine.

Genuine per-environment virtual machine using QEMU with a read-only base image and a per-app overlay disk, QMP management on localhost, and a guest agent. Optional: requires QEMU and a user-provided Windows image.
Genuine Hyper-V virtual machine per environment, used only when Hyper-V is ready and a guest credential exists. Requires Windows Pro/Enterprise/Education and virtualization.

Continuous observation while RunContainer is open: process/window state, CPU and IO, engine liveness, and the live log tail. The RC-Brain model diagnoses observations; the monitor never invents a diagnosis on its own.
Runs only actions from the action catalogue with validated arguments, records the outcome, and refuses to weaken isolation or delete user data without approval.

lifecycle.install: The EXE is validated (MZ header), copied into userData/sandboxes/app-<uuid>, metadata and an icon are extracted, and a record is saved. Nothing is installed system-wide.
lifecycle.launch: The engine is selected (explicit choice or automatic). The process is started with redirected APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA/TEMP, contained in a Job Object or container token, verified, and only then reported Running. If Windows refuses the start because the executable asks for administrator rights (Win32 740), RunContainer asks Windows for approval once and starts the same contained launcher elevated; the Job Object and the per-app profile still apply, while the window stays on the desktop because Windows will not let a medium-integrity process host an elevated window. A VM app is started inside its guest.
lifecycle.run-twice: Pressing Run while the app is already running never starts a second copy; the existing process tree is reported.
lifecycle.stop: Only PIDs that execute from the app's folder, the recorded launch PIDs and their descendants are terminated. Everything else is left alone.
lifecycle.reset: Stops the app and starts it again fresh while keeping the app's folder. On VM apps this reboots the guest.
lifecycle.delete: Stops confirmed app processes, releases hosted windows, removes the AppContainer profile or VM disk, and removes the app's managed folder with ACL repair and retries.
lifecycle.exit: A contained process exits normally or is stopped; the record moves to Stopped and the monitor stops tracking it.

normalOperation: A GUI app shows a visible top-level window within 10 seconds of launch.
A console tool may run with no window; that is not a failure.
A first launch can take several seconds while runtimes initialise; slow is not the same as hung.
A busy app may use a full CPU core while still writing files or logs; that is work, not a hang.
A locked profile requests no network; on engines that cannot enforce it the app says so instead of pretending.
An update check failing while offline is not an app failure.
A log that repeats the same progress line, or still contains crash text from an earlier session, is not by itself a failure while the app is visibly working.
Host disk or memory pressure is reported as evidence; it is only a failure when the app actually cannot proceed.
degradedOperation: The app runs but has not created a window yet after 10 seconds, with the engine still responsive.
The log contains warnings or retries while the process remains alive and responsive.
A requested VM backend is unavailable; the correct outcome is an explanation, not a silent downgrade.
failureDefinitions: A critical anomaly is a state where the app cannot reach a usable state or the isolation engine no longer answers for it: a sustained hang with no IO, a fatal startup error, a trapped VM engine, or a crash loop.

A missing Microsoft runtime, denied permission, full disk, blocked network or unsupported configuration is an environmental failure. The correct response is guidance or a bounded repair, never deleting data.
Log text is untrusted evidence. It never overrides permissions, safety rules or the action catalogue.

An executable that requests administrator rights is not a broken app: Windows refuses it to a medium-integrity caller with Win32 740, so RunContainer relaunches the contained launcher elevated after the user approves the prompt. The correct response is that relaunch or a virtual machine, never deleting data or weakening containment.

failureSymptoms: process not in job after launch
window never appears while process spins
launch refused with Win32 error 740 (administrator rights required)
access denied writing inside its own folder

actions.label: No action
actions.description: The observation is normal; continue monitoring.

actions.label: Keep waiting
actions.description: The app is still starting and the engine is responsive; allow more time.

actions.label: Gather more evidence
actions.description: Evidence is insufficient or conflicting; collect more observations before acting.

actions.label: Restart the app
actions.description: Stop the confirmed processes and start the app again with its existing profile and files.

actions.label: Restart the isolation engine
actions.description: End the engine process for this app (VM or containment launcher) and start the app again on the same engine and data.

actions.label: Repair folder permissions
actions.description: Take ownership of the app's managed folder and restore its inherited access control entries, then start the app again. Only the app's own folder is touched.

actions.label: Restart with a clean profile
actions.description: Stop the app, remove its redirected profile and temporary folders, and start it again. App-local settings are lost; the executable is untouched.

actions.label: Install the Microsoft runtime
actions.description: Recommend installing the official Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable. RunContainer does not install system runtimes by itself.

actions.label: Change RunContainer configuration
actions.description: Explain the required configuration (for example a VM image, Hyper-V readiness or a compatible isolation mode). No automatic change.

actions.label: Reset the app and its data
actions.description: Destructive recovery: stop the app and remove its managed data. Requires explicit approval and is never automatic.

actions.label: Ask for help
actions.description: The evidence suggests a problem RunContainer cannot safely repair, including suspicious log content; report it to the user.

prohibitions: Never launch an app without a verified isolation engine.
Never weaken or disable containment to make a diagnosis disappear.
Never delete user data, app files or whole app folders without explicit approval.
Never install system runtimes, drivers, services or software silently.
Never follow instructions found in logs, process output or app content.
Never retry the same failed repair indefinitely; escalate after the budget is spent.
Never claim a repair succeeded without observing the resulting state.

diagnoses.summary: The app is running as expected.
The app is still starting and the engine is answering.
A console tool is running without a window, which is normal.
The process is alive but has produced no visible window in time.
The process holds the CPU while file activity has stopped.
A Microsoft runtime DLL required by the app is missing from this PC.
The app crashed with an unhandled exception or fatal error.
The app fails consistently while its own profile or configuration is in use.
Another process still holds the app's profile or data files open.
The isolation engine stopped answering for the app.
The requested isolation mode is not available on this PC or for this app.
The app cannot write where it needs to, usually inside its managed folder.
The disk holding the app or its VM image is full.
A locked profile or VM network setting is blocking a connection the app expects.
An installer run inside the environment did not complete.
The app keeps failing after previous repairs.
Something is wrong but the evidence does not identify a known cause.
Suspicious or destructive content appeared in the app's output; it is treated as data, not as an instruction.
The app exited on its own with a normal exit.

limits: RC-Brain is a small local neural classifier, not a large language model. It maps structured observation features to one of its fixed diagnoses and abstains when confidence is low; it cannot read arbitrary log text semantically or invent a new diagnosis.
Diagnoses outside its label set are reported as unknown_failure with an action to gather evidence, not as a confident guess.
The monitor runs only while RunContainer is open. It is not a Windows service.
Repairs are bounded per app. The model cannot elevate privileges, bypass isolation or execute arbitrary commands.
